name: secure-error-handling
description: Handle errors securely without leaking stack traces, internal paths, database details, or system information to users
author: community
content:
## Secure Error Handling

Errors are for developers. Users get friendly messages. Attackers get nothing useful (OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design).

### Rules
- NEVER expose stack traces, internal paths, database errors, or SQL queries to end users
- Return generic error messages to clients: "Something went wrong" or "Request failed"
- Log full error details server-side with correlation IDs
- Return a correlation/request ID to the client so support can look up the full error
- Use different error detail levels per environment: verbose in development, minimal in production
- Catch all unhandled exceptions at the top level — do not let frameworks show default error pages
- Do not include internal IP addresses, server names, or software versions in responses
- Do not differentiate between "user not found" and "wrong password" — use generic auth errors

### What NOT to Return to Users
```json
// BAD — leaks internals
{
  "error": "PG::UndefinedTable: ERROR: relation \"users\" does not exist",
  "stack": "at /app/src/models/user.rb:42\n at /app/src/controllers/auth.rb:15",
  "query": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@company.com'"
}

// GOOD — safe error response
{
  "error": "An unexpected error occurred.",
  "request_id": "req_a1b2c3d4"
}
```

### Server-Side Logging (DO log these)
```
[ERROR] [req_a1b2c3d4] [2026-03-23T10:15:30Z] PG::UndefinedTable: relation "users" does not exist
  at /app/src/models/user.rb:42
  at /app/src/controllers/auth.rb:15
  user_id=anonymous ip=192.168.1.1 endpoint=POST /api/login
```

### Framework Configuration

#### Express.js
```javascript
// Global error handler — must be last middleware
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  const requestId = req.id;
  logger.error({ err, requestId, path: req.path });
  res.status(err.status || 500).json({
    error: 'An unexpected error occurred.',
    request_id: requestId
  });
});
```

#### Django
```python
# settings.py
DEBUG = False  # NEVER True in production

# Custom error handler
def handler500(request):
    return JsonResponse({'error': 'An unexpected error occurred.'}, status=500)
```

#### Go
```go
func errorHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
    reqID := r.Context().Value("request_id")
    log.Error().Err(err).Str("request_id", reqID).Msg("unhandled error")
    http.Error(w, `{"error":"An unexpected error occurred."}`, 500)
}
```

### Common Information Leaks
- Server headers: remove `X-Powered-By`, `Server` headers in production
- Debug endpoints: disable `/debug`, `/status`, `/health` endpoints that expose internals
- Error pages: replace default framework error pages (Django debug, Express stack traces)
- API documentation: do not expose Swagger/OpenAPI in production unless intentional
- Source maps: do not deploy source maps to production
